{text:body}

A lot of Logan homes went up in the 80s and 90s, and the concrete tiles on them are now 30 to 40 years old. At that age the ridge capping has usually cracked, the bedding mortar has crumbled and the tile coating has worn off, so most of our Logan work is repointing and restoration, which costs far less than a new roof. Around Daisy Hill and Shailer Park the bushland drops a steady load of leaves and gum nuts into gutters and valleys, and that is where many of the leaks we find begin. Beenleigh and the older streets near the Logan River have more timber homes with metal roofs. Those tend to need new screws, fresh flashings and the odd rusted sheet replaced. Summer storms roll through most years, and after a bad one we put tarping and emergency repairs for Logan customers at the front of the queue. We're in Logan most weeks, so an inspection is usually only a couple of days away.
